The `sha256sums` entry is present and verified, ensuring the integrity of the downloaded source.

The `prepare()`, `build()`, and `package()` functions are not executed due to the `--noprepare` and `--nobuild` flags, so any potentially risky operations within them (such as `fvm` invocations or patch applications) are not triggered at this stage.

No network requests, data exfiltration, or code execution occurs during the sourcing of this PKGBUILD or source download that would compromise safety. All operations are consistent with standard AUR packaging practices.
</details>

<details>
The provided <.SRCINFO> file contains metadata for the saber package from the Arch User Repository. It declares standard package information including version, architecture, dependencies, source URL, and checksums. The source is fetched from the official GitHub repository (https://github.com/saber-notes/saber) at a specific tagged release (v1.36.1), which is a common and acceptable practice for AUR packages. The SHA-256 checksum is explicitly listed and matches the expected value for the release tarball, indicating that the source integrity can be verified.

All listed dependencies are standard system libraries commonly required by GUI applications on Linux, such as GTK, WebKit, Cairo, and GLib. There are no signs of obfuscated commands, suspicious network operations, or unexpected file manipulations in this metadata file. The makedepends include typical build tools like cmake, clang, rustup, and fvm (Flutter Version Manager), which aligns with the upstream project's use of Flutter and Rust for development.

This file does not contain executable code, scripts, or any logic that could be exploited for supply chain attacks. It serves only as declarative packaging metadata used by Arch Linux's build system. No evidence of malicious behavior or deviation from standard AUR packaging practices was found.
</details>

<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD appears to be a standard Arch Linux package build script for the "saber" note-taking application. It fetches the source from the project's official GitHub repository using a tagged release archive (v1.36.1), which is a common and acceptable practice. The checksum provided (sha256sums) matches the expected value for that release, indicating integrity verification is in place.

The build process uses `fvm` (Flutter Version Manager) to pin the Flutter SDK version, which enhances reproducibility. It runs two patch scripts (`remove_permission_handler.sh` and `remove_proprietary_dependencies.sh`) located within the source tree under `./patches/pre/`. These are likely used to remove non-free or unnecessary components, which is consistent with Arch packaging policies favoring open-source software. Since these scripts are part of the fetched source and not downloaded externally at build time, and given their described purpose aligns with typical AUR maintainer modifications, they do not raise red flags.

No network operations, code downloads, obfuscated commands, or suspicious file manipulations occur during build or package phases. The installation uses standard commands (`install`, `cp`, `ln -s`) to place files in appropriate system directories. Metadata files (desktop, icon, metainfo) are installed as expected. There is no evidence of data exfiltration, backdoors, or execution of external code.
</details>
